scenes.heading: Pricing design work: hourly vs. project vs. value-based

sents.d: Pricing design work: hourly vs. project vs. value-based
Each pricing model fits different types of design work.
Hourly pricing is simple but penalizes speed and experience — a fast, skilled designer earns less per project than a slower one billing the same hourly rate for more hours.

Project-based pricing (a flat fee for a defined scope) rewards efficiency and gives clients cost certainty, but requires clearly defining what's included so added requests don't quietly expand the work for free.

Value-based pricing — pricing based on the business impact of the work rather than time spent — works best for clients where the design clearly drives revenue (a logo for a funded startup versus a flyer for a local bake sale), and usually takes more experience to price confidently.

take: Match your pricing model to the client and the impact of the work.
